subject.title: Core hardening tracker: converge duplicated runtime invariants onto single owners

question: Which remaining canonical-owner seam should be sponsored after the active error-classification slice?
rationale: The remaining rows differ materially in user impact, compatibility sensitivity, and architectural risk, so source duplication alone cannot determine their sequence or permanent owner boundary.

options.title: Sequence narrow rows
options.body: Sponsor one independently verified seam at a time, prioritizing demonstrated drift and requiring owner-specific proof before implementation.

options.title: Narrow the tracker
options.body: Retain only rows with demonstrated user-visible or reliability drift and move lower-priority type or cleanup ideas to separate discussions.

options.title: Pause after active slice
options.body: Complete the open error-classification slice and defer all other rows until a concrete regression or maintainer need appears.

recommendation.title: Sequence narrow rows
recommendation.body: Sponsor one independently verified seam at a time, prioritizing demonstrated drift and requiring owner-specific proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest merged-history context across the completed slices and the active follow-up, though final sponsorship remains a maintainer decision.
